text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

After suffering at the hands of the South African pace attack, the Australian cricket team has fought itself back into the third cricket Test in Port Elizabeth. Paceman Jason Gillespie continued his good form, taking 3 for 36 to have the South Africans sx for 137 at lunch. Page 25.

The Australian cycling community was dealt a major blow last night after it was confirmed triple Commonwealth gold medallist Gary Neiwand tested positive for the banned drug pseudoephedrine. Neiwand will not be banned from competition, but will face a $A000 fine. Page 25.

Saturday saw the emergence of yet another swimming star at the Pan-Pacific trials in Adelaide -- 14-year-old Ian Thorpe. Thorpe has been recognised as the fastest swimmer for his age in history and will represent Australia at the Pan Pacific championships in te 400 metres in Japan in August. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Canberra Raider's horror run in the Super League competition continued yesterday as they were mauled 38-26 by the Canterbury Bulldogs. The Raiders once again turned in a woeful defensive performance for their third straight loss of the season, leaving the competition favourites languishing at the bottom of the table. Page 27.

The New South Wales cricket team won the battle but failed to win the war in their Sheffield Shield match against Tasmania at the SCG yesterday. The Blues batted magnificently to reach the target of 305 set by the Tasmanians, which left them with 28 poins. However, they were squeezed out of next week's final by Queensland, whose four outright wins and superior run quotient took them into the final against Western Australia on Thursday. Page 29.

Hockeyroos coach Ric Charlesworth was unconvinced with his side's 4-2 victory against Germany at Homebush yesterday. Charlesworth cited improvements in the Olympic champion team's fitness, combinations and enthusiasm as the major goals for this. Page 30
THE AGE

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco has been buoyed by the news that one of the witnesses to give evidence against him in his fight to clear his name of drugs charges has withdrawn part of his evidence. The news came during the second day of hearings befre the International Amateur Athletics Federation which is to decide if Capobianco should be banned after testing positive for steroids in Holland last year. Page10.

Carlton flanker Simon Beaumont will know this week if he will play in next weekend's Ansett Cup final against Geelong after being charged with kicking an opponent in the Blues' game against St Kilda on Saturday night. The Australian Football Tribunal wil hear the case either tonight or tomorrow. Page 7.

Australian skiing sensation Kirstie Marshall won her fifth world cup event of the season in Sweden during the weekend but it was not enough to overhaul Canadian Veronica Brener for this year's World Cup title. Marshall, who scored 163 during the weekend ompetition has dominated since Christmas, but has not been able to overtake the Canadian. Page 16.
THE HERALD SUN

Port Power's number 1 signing Gavin Wanganeen is in danger of missing the first Australian Football League match for the new club after being reported for striking in a practice match against Richmond. Wanganeen, who was taken form the field immediately after the report, could find himself in further trouble after grabbing the umpire who booked the 23-year-old defender. Page 74.

South Melbourne soccer team squandered its chance to move into second position in the Ericsson Cup after losing 1-0 in the local derby against South Melbourne. The Knight's goal came in the 29th minute after goalkeeper Mike Petkovic failed to secure an icoming cross which was headed in at the far post by striker Adrian Cervinski. Page 72.

Australian golfer Craig Parry shot a course record eight-under-par 64 to move only five strokes from the lead in the second round of the Honda Classic at Fort Lauderdale in Florida. Countryman Stuart Appleby remains the best placed Australian, leaving him in seventh position and only three strokes off the lead. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Sydney Kings recorded their first victory in the NBL cup with a convincing 113-82 victory against the Canberra Cannons in Canberra. The win, which keeps their final hopes alive, was a boost to the team after suffering a disheartening 110-104 loss to he Illawarra Hawks. Page 28.

The North Sydney Bears had to struggle to beat the 12-man Newcastle team 34-20 in Sydney yesterday after Newcastle captain Matthew Johns was sent off in the fifth minute after an alleged high tackle against Scott Pethybridge. If Matthew is suspended, it will be the first time the Knights have had to play without the influential Johns brothers in four years. Page 31.

Former motorcycle champion Wayne Gardiner scored his first win in the Australian Touring Car Championships with a victory at the Calder Park raceway on Saturday night. Gardiner, who combined his win in the second race with two second placings during the ight, was followed by Ford driver Glen Seton and Holden's Russell Ingall. Page 41.
